target_customer: Software engineers looking for jobs by team culture, and companies that pay to be listed and featured
problem: Developers cannot easily see what a team's culture and values are like before applying.
business_model: Paid job listings and recruiting services for companies; free for job seekers
product_category: Culture-focused tech job board and recruiting

founders.name: Lynne Tye
education: MIT (2010, brain and cognitive sciences, self-reported)
founders.background_notes: Education from her own dev.to profile, a self-reported source.

technical_complexity.rationale: A content and job board website; the difficulty was in collecting and verifying culture data from teams, not engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Job boards and company culture pages are easy to copy; the only asset is curated interview content and founder reputation.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Stack Overflow announced in January 2022 that it would sunset Jobs; no sign any incumbent copied Key Values specifically.

market_need_then: Founder says on dev.to the site aims to give job seekers a way to find like-minded teams and give teams a benchmark against the industry; no hard demand data found.

branding.community_and_virality: Founder engages with developers on dev.to; no merch or press on the brand found.

brand_strength.rationale: Little evidence beyond developer community posts and aggregator profiles.

outcome_analysis: Key Values remains a very small, mostly solo company that has stayed active since its Winter 2018 batch. Aggregators report roughly 350 thousand dollars in annual revenue, which suggests a small durable business rather than a venture scale outcome, and no shutdown or acquisition was found. The sources are thin, so the real cause of its modest scale is not public.
notes: keyvalues.com returned HTTP 503 on fetch, so the site could not be read. Funding seen only in aggregator snippets: CB Insights lists about $150K convertible note from Y Combinator dated 2018-01-01 (possibly a placeholder date), unverified so no round recorded. Revenue claims ($350K per year attributed to a 2019 Indie Hackers podcast, $360K in November 2023) come from GetLatka and are unverified. No competitor sources dated near 2018 found. Founding year not stated in sources. Name origin not found.
